events.credibility_reason: Content known only from search excerpts; the meaning of 'basis' and the characteristic scope could not be checked.

events.ai_basis: Using ChatGPT 5.6, we find a counterexample to the stable forking conjecture.

why: The statement asks only about characteristic zero, so Wagner's positive-characteristic theorem is a variant, not a case. Krupinski-Tanovic-Wagner (unordered minimal fields), Fukuzaki (infinite basis) and Gogacz-Krupinski (generically stable regular fields) each settle a class of objects and are cases, all before the snapshot; none resolves the question, and the record itself quotes KTW calling characteristic zero wide open. The only in-window items are Johnson-Tran-Walsberg-Ye, which at most reduces Podewski to an open topology question (none), and Freitag-Mutchnik, which is about the stable forking conjecture, a different problem (variant). Its AI role is answered from its own abstract quote as assisted rather than generated because a news report says the humans wrote the proofs; it is discarded either way.
doubts: Gogacz-Krupinski as a 'case' is a close call: it proves a generalized conjecture for generically stable regular fields, and it is not established which minimal fields of characteristic zero fall under that; it could be read as variant. No effect on status since it predates the snapshot and is not whole. In-window arXiv coverage was approximated via a general web index.
